messages:
John D. (customer): Hey team — starting ~09:27 UTC we're seeing spikes of 502/504 from the hosted inference endpoints for our prod app. Only noticed after a deploy window but looks like TLS/connectivity issues. Samples: curl -> 502 Gateway. Request-Id: rq_0a1b2c3d.

John D. (customer): Quick repro (I can share more if needed):
```bash
curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-...\" \"https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate?model=redwood-13b\" -d '{"prompt":"hi","max_tokens":10}'
```

John D. (customer): curl shows TLS handshake timeout on a few attempts: `recv TLS handshake: timeout` and sometimes `SSL: certificate verify failed`.

Alejandra (support): Sorry you're hitting this — we're on it. Can you paste the `x-redwood-request-id` header from one of the failing responses? Also which region/edge (us-east-1, etc) and approx timestamps?

John D. (customer): request-id: `rq_0a1b2c3d` (that's from 2024-02-17T09:27:13Z). Region reported from client: `us-east-1`. We pushed a small model config change at 09:20 but traffic surge is low.

Matt (oncall): I pulled the request id — seeing a chain of 502s from our gateway with underlying error `upstream read timeout` and intermittent `tls: handshake did not complete` on the resolver path. Dropped packets to resolver not super high but there are resolver SERVFAILs around same window.

Helena (infra): Noted. Can you run a quick dig + traceroute from your client host to our api domain and paste output? Also, `openssl s_client -connect api.redwood-inference.com:443 -servername api.redwood-inference.com -tlsextdebug` would be helpful.

John D. (customer): Pasted results:
```
$ dig +short api.redwood-inference.com @8.8.8.8
104.21.32.99
104.21.33.100

$ dig +short api.redwood-inference.com @my-corp-resolver
; communication error to my-corp-resolver#53: connection timed out

$ traceroute api.redwood-inference.com
traceroute to api.redwood-inference.com (104.21.32.99), 30 hops max
 1  10.0.0.1  1.2 ms
 ...
 7  * * *
 8  192.0.2.5  42 ms
```

John D. (customer): `openssl s_client` output sometimes returns the cert chain but other times fails in handshake with `no peer certificate`.

Alejandra (support): Hmm looks like their corporate resolver is flaky (connection timed out) and traceroute shows hop 7 dropping. Could be intermittent DNS latency causing our edge to select a different resolver path or degrade. We'll check our edge resolver metrics for SERVFAIL/SERVRESET spikes.

dns-bot: Observability alert — dns-resolver-us-east spike: 2024-02-17T09:26:30Z to 09:29:00Z: SERVFAIL rate 12% (baseline 0.2%).

Matt (oncall): Confirmed in edge logs: resolver backends returned SERVFAIL and we had fallback to alternate resolver pool which had higher egress latency. That, combined with an ongoing OCSP stapling delay on a small subset of edge nodes (post-cert refresh), amplified handshake timeouts.

Helena (infra): We're seeing a brief cert rotation event at 09:25:40Z — `deploy-bot: edge-cert-rollout started` across canary nodes, and OCSP responders for one CA had a 20s delay for stapling at the same time. Those two things together explain intermittent `certificate verify failed` and `handshake timeout` errors downstream.

Alejandra (support): TL;DR — two contributing factors: (1) transient resolver SERVFAILs in the us-east resolver pool causing client requests to take a slow/fallback path, (2) a short OCSP stapling delay on a subset of edge nodes during our cert rotation. Both caused gateway-level 502/504. We're rolling a mitigation.

Matt (oncall): Mitigation steps taken:
- Rebalanced resolver pool to healthy nodes (manual cutover at 09:33).
- Paused certificate rollout to remaining rows to let OCSP caches warm.
- Increased handshake timeout threshold temporarily to reduce 502s while we stabilize.

Helena (infra): Patch pushed to decrease handshake aggressiveness:
```yaml
edge.conn.handshake_timeout: 12s  # Was 6s temporarily bumped to 12s
edge.dns.fallback_ttl_ms: 120  # reduce aggressive fallback frequency
```

Helena (infra): Also added retry-on-SERVFAIL in resolver client with jitter for 2s window to avoid flapping.

John D. (customer): Thanks — saw errors drop after ~09:34. We'll keep an eye and run a few load tests. Will you follow up with root cause and next steps?

Alejandra (support): Absolutely. We'll keep the incident open until end of day and share a short RCA. For now: please collect a couple of failing curl outputs if you see them again and ping this thread. :thumbsup:

Matt (oncall): Postmortem notes to add: brief resolver instability (internal AS-level peering flaps) + simultaneous OCSP stapling delay during cert refresh. Mitigations: stagger cert rollouts, add OCSP cache warming step, add resolver health check gating for rollouts.

dns-bot: deploy-bot: edge-cert-rollout completed for canary at 09:39:02Z. No further OCSP delays observed after 09:41Z.

John D. (customer): Confirming recovery — 200 responses now, latency back to normal. Thanks everyone for fast triage.

Alejandra (support): Thanks for the quick repro and patience. We'll follow up with a short RCA doc and any recommended client-side mitigations (e.g., DNS resolver fallback, certificate chain verification logs).
